title: Delegated Sink Orchestration for On-Prem Observability with Tenant-Scoped Replay
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Goal: Implement a delegated sink orchestration layer for on-prem/VPC collectors that enables per-tenant replay buffers, tenant-scoped routing, and backpressure-aware handoff to Redwood central ingestion. This ticket covers design, prototype, and rollout plan for: 1) a lightweight delegated sink controller running in customer private clusters that manages ephemeral outbound relays; 2) tenant-scoped replay queues with durable boundaries and watermarking; 3) an adaptive backpressure protocol that signals rate limits to local collectors and triggers replay fallback to local durable storage when central uplink is constrained.

Rationale: Current on-prem collectors drop or delay telemetry during central outages or heavy spikes, causing cross-tenant contamination risk and opaque failure modes for Dedicated/Private customers. The delegated sink and tenant-scoped replay approach preserves tenant isolation, reduces central load spikes, and gives predictable recovery behavior for bounded windows of time.

Success criteria: - Per-tenant replay buffer with configurable retention and byte/entry caps; - No cross-tenant telemetry visibility during replay or failover; - Central uplink can signal polite backpressure and collectors throttle without data loss for up to configured retention; - End-to-end integration test and a canary rollout plan for 3 pilot customers; - Dashboarding and alerts for replay events, ingress backpressure, and per-tenant dropped-event rates.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by SRE and Security
End-to-end integration test covering central outage simulation passes
Pilot rollout to two Dedicated customers with throttling profiles documented
No cross-tenant leakage verified by automated property tests
Dashboards surfaced in Console: tenant-replay-heatmap, ingress-uplink-latency, per-tenant-drop-rate
updates: 2026-02-10: Ticket opened. Initial scope and rationale captured. Assigned to Liam. Blockers: need security review early due to on-prem storage of telemetry.

2026-02-12: Spike completed: prototyped a local ring buffer persisted to disk using append-only WAL. Found WAL compaction trade-offs (latency vs. disk wear). Decision: use chunked segment files with CRC checksums to make replay robust to unclean shutdowns.

2026-02-15: Architecture sync with SRE and Security. Security insisted on tenant-keyed envelope signing for replay segments. Added envelope signing to scope; will use customer-managed KMS where available or a cluster-local ephemeral key otherwise.

2026-02-18: Implemented control-plane handshake for delegated sink controller. Controller issues outbound credentials to collectors and rotates ephemeral tokens every 6 hours. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/collector-proto/pull/642 (WIP).

2026-02-20: Backpressure protocol draft: central-ingest returns 429 with structured hints {retryAfterMs, preferredBatchSize}, collectors apply PID-based leaky-bucket throttling and begin draining to local replay. Trade-off: aggressive throttling reduces central tail latency but increases local disk usage. Using conservative defaults for pilot.

2026-02-23: Integration test harness extension: added central outage simulator that blackholes uplinks and verifies replay persists to disk and is reconciled on recovery. Initial run passed for 10k events at 50MB retention; failing case observed when segment count hits file-descriptor limits — action: add FD recycling and segment compaction.

2026-02-26: Design doc published in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Delegated+Sink+and+Tenant+Replay. Requesting security review and performance benchmarks before scheduling pilot.

2026-02-28: Design review notes: PM asked to expose tenant-level retention knobs in Console; UX will add a compact policy editor. SRE recommends additional metrics: per-tenant replay-latency-p50/p95 and local-disk-pressure. Added to metric list.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: On-disk replay can leak tenant contexts if segments are mis-indexed. Mitigation: strict per-tenant segment naming, signed envelopes, and a verification pass during replay acceptance.

Risk: Local disk saturation causing collector crash. Mitigation: configurable low-watermark eviction and oldest-segment purge, plus alerting and optional remote-tiering to customer-managed S3-compatible stores.
Risk: Central backpressure signals may be noisy and cause oscillation. Mitigation: hysteresis on throttle adjustments and load-aware smoothing (exponential backoff with jitter).
